_comment: Mutations for the CameraNode registration and heartbeat slice. These two routes carry more branching than anything ported so far — a version gate, a camera reconciliation, a debounced alert and a recording map — and none of it was ever compared before, because both were proxied: the differential was running Python against Python and scoring it green. The filter is this slice's own cases; a full sweep is 702 cases. The plan-cap half lives in node_register_cap.json, against the Clerk-mode pair, because it is unreachable under the local auth these tiers run.

mutations.name: the port default is dropped
mutations._why: `Field(8080, ...)` on an Optional[int] applies its default when the key is ABSENT, which is every register a node sends that does not mention a port. Treating absent as None leaves the column alone instead of setting 8080 — and this is exactly what the first run of this slice got wrong, on seventeen cases at once.
mutations.old:
let http_port = match body.get("http_port") {
        None => Some(8080),
mutations.new:
let http_port = match body.get("http_port") {
        None => None,

mutations.name: the returned key is decoded as UTF-8
mutations._why: Starlette decodes header bytes as latin-1. `node_secret` hands the key back to the node, and a lossy UTF-8 decode replaces any high byte with U+FFFD — handing back a key that will not authenticate.
mutations.old: let api_key_text: String = key.iter().map(|&b| b as char).collect();

mutations.name: the version is persisted before the gate
mutations._why: The heartbeat raises out of the 426 with nothing committed, so the version columns it assigned roll back. Writing them first leaves a refused node looking like it reported successfully. Registration is the opposite — its error recorder commits — and a port that treats both the same is wrong on one of them.
mutations.old: // The version columns are written only once the gate passes.

mutations.name: an absent version stores 0.0.0
mutations._why: `version_check["parsed"] if data.node_version else None`. A node too old to report a version must leave the column NULL, not claim to be running 0.0.0 — the dashboard tells those apart.

mutations.name: zero free bytes is treated as a full disk
mutations._why: CameraNode reports disk_free_bytes = 0 when it could not identify the disk, which Python's `not free_bytes` catches along with None. Reading it as a genuine zero alerts every containerised node that it is 100% full.

mutations.name: the disk-low anchor is never cleared
mutations._why: Crossing back under the threshold clears the debounce so the next crossing alerts at once. Leaving it set means a node that recovers and fills again stays silent for up to six hours.

mutations.name: the disk-low debounce is ignored
a malformed disk anchor blocks the alert
mutations._why: Python catches the ValueError and falls through to emit, then overwrites the bad value. Treating a parse failure as "recently emitted" would let one hand-edited row silence a node's disk alerts permanently.

mutations.name: unreported cameras are left behind
mutations._why: A device that is unplugged, renamed, or re-sanitised leaves its old row and its segment cache forever.

mutations.name: the stale camera's cache is kept
mutations._why: The row goes and the memory does not. Nothing in the database shows it, which is why this is worth a mutation of its own.
mutations.equivalent: The write differential snapshots tables, and the segment cache is memory. hls_run.sh covers the cache, but it has no registration case — the two harnesses do not meet here.

mutations.name: an empty capability list is stored as empty
mutations._why: `",".join(caps) if caps else "streaming"` — an empty list is falsy in Python and takes the default.

mutations.name: lan_streaming=False does not clear the ip
mutations._why: A loopback-bound node whose local_ip survives hands Home Assistant a stream URL that refuses the connection.

mutations.name: an absent lan_streaming clears the ip
mutations._why: The tri-state matters: None is an old CameraNode that does not know the field, and must keep the legacy behaviour rather than be treated as False.

mutations.name: the cap sweep is skipped on register
mutations._why: The safety net for an org whose subscription webhook never arrived. Without it their flags stay stale forever, because nothing else recomputes them.

mutations.name: the past-due sweep runs for everyone
mutations._why: Gating on the flag is what keeps the happy path free — but running it always is also observably different, because it recomputes caps on every heartbeat of every org.

mutations.name: the past-due sweep never runs
a healthy camera keeps its last error
mutations._why: A recovered camera that still shows why it failed an hour ago is worse than one showing nothing.

mutations.name: a camera on another node is updated
mutations._why: The node_id filter is the tenant boundary here: a node must not be able to mark another node's cameras failed by naming them.
mutations.equivalent: The pre-check is belt-and-braces: the UPDATE below carries `AND node_id = $5` itself, so dropping the lookup changes which rows are CONSIDERED and not which are written. The mutation below removes the WHERE clause instead, which is where the boundary actually lives.

mutations.name: the badge plan is resolved instead of read
mutations._why: Heartbeats are every thirty seconds per node, and resolve_org_plan calls Clerk for any org whose cached slug is not paid. The Setting is deliberately authoritative here.

mutations.name: disabled cameras are reported org-wide
mutations._why: Scoped to this node's cameras. A sibling node's suspended camera in the list tells this node to stop pushing a stream it does not own.
mutations.old: FROM cameras WHERE node_id = $1 ORDER BY id
mutations.new: FROM cameras WHERE org_id = (SELECT org_id FROM camera_nodes WHERE id = $1) ORDER BY id

mutations.name: continuous recording is ignored
a schedule with no times records always
an unparseable window records always
mutations._why: Python's int() raises and the caller catches it, which means do-not-record. Recording on a parse failure is the failure mode that fills a disk.

mutations.name: a bad timezone raises instead of falling back
mutations._why: An exception here would 500 every heartbeat for that org and stop its recording entirely, which is why Python falls back to UTC.

mutations.name: the key check runs before validation
mutations._why: FastAPI validates the body before the handler body runs at all, so a request with no key AND a bad body answers 422, not 401. Checking the key first inverts that on every malformed request.

mutations.name: nested errors report at the top level
mutations._why: The loc is what the SPA reads to highlight a field. `["body", "cameras", 0, "name"]` and `["body", "name"]` are different messages to a user and different summaries in the envelope.

mutations.name: a non-object camera reports as dict_type
mutations._why: Pydantic distinguishes a model from a dict: a model would also accept an arbitrary object and read attributes off it, and says so.

mutations.name: the update does not scope to the node
mutations._why: This is the tenant boundary, not the pre-check above it. Without the node_id in the WHERE, a node can mark any camera in any org failed by naming it — the camera_id is the only other term, and it is global.
mutations.old: "UPDATE cameras SET status = $1, last_seen = $2, last_error = $3, updated_at = $2\n                  WHERE camera_id = $4 AND node_id = $5",
mutations.new: "UPDATE cameras SET status = $1, last_seen = $2, last_error = $3, updated_at = $2\n                  WHERE camera_id = $4 AND $5 = $5",
